sections.h2: Where an Adams County deed gets recorded
sections.html:
Land records for the county are kept in West Union. Bring a deed or mortgage to 110 West Main Street, Room 133, West Union, OH 45693. Two phone lines are posted on the county's recorder page, 937-544-5051 and 937-544-2513. Weekday service ends at 4 in the afternoon.

You can also look up filed documents on the Adams County public access portal. Make an account first, since the portal wants a username and password. It also sells an alert service for new filings against a parcel, which some owners use to catch fraud early.

Most sellers never carry the deed themselves, since the closing agent usually does. Still, knowing the route helps you read the charges on your settlement statement.

The legislature, not the county, fixes what the recorder may charge. Section 317.32 pairs every base fee with an equal housing trust fund fee. For a standard instrument the first two pages cost $17 plus $17. Every further sheet, legal size or any part of one and counting the caption page, adds $4 plus $4.

A preservation surcharge, capped at $5 an instrument, may be added on top and is kept by the county. Ohio law sets a cap only, so call the recorder for Adams County's actual figure before you bring a check.

Payment is due at the counter when the paper is handed in. Electronic filers can settle later by bank transfer. Count the pages in your deed before you go, since every page past the second adds to the bill.

In Ohio, the auditor sees a deed before the recorder does. Under section 319.202, the person receiving title, or someone acting for that person, files a statement of value. That can be done online or on three paper copies. Next the auditor marks the deed with the fee taken and a notation that the filing was made. Then it moves to the recorder.

Two charges can land on the seller here:

  • The conveyance fee under section 319.54(G)(3): $1 or ten cents per hundred dollars of value, whichever is larger, with a partial hundred rounded up.
  • A county real property transfer tax, which applies only if the commissioners adopted one under section 322.02. It tops out at thirty cents per hundred dollars and falls on the grantor.

Ask the auditor, at 937-544-2364, if the optional tax is in force here. Numbers for other offices: treasurer 937-544-2317, commissioners 937-544-3286, clerk of courts title department 937-544-2345.

sections.h2: Transfers exempt from the conveyance fee
sections.html:
The auditor's fee has carve-outs, and many involve family. A gift between spouses qualifies, and so does a gift from a parent to a child or the child's spouse. Heirs or devisees of one estate who trade property without paying for it are covered too. So is a deed placing land into a trust that the maker can revoke at will, and a deed whose only job is to correct or confirm an earlier recorded one. Transfers made solely to secure a debt, or to release that security, are also excused, as are transactions with no money or other value changing hands that are not gifts, and any interest worth $100 or less.

If your transfer qualifies, the filing must give the reason. The recorder's own charges still apply to an exempt deed, so budget for them.

sections.h2: Tax reductions and the statement of value
sections.html:
This filing connects the sale to the tax bill. The buyer either affirms that the seller reported no reduction of the prior or current year's taxes under section 323.152, or attaches a sworn instrument showing the estimated reduction. A parcel with farm-use valuation needs a similar affirmation about the current agricultural use value and any recoupment charge.

Find out what reductions your parcel carries before closing. The auditor's office can tell you, and the same 937-544-2364 number takes questions about CAUV farm valuation.

sections.h2: Selling fast or selling an inherited house
sections.html:
A cash sale follows the standard sequence. The deed is signed, the auditor receives the statement of value, and the recorder files the deed in West Union. Title companies normally handle the runs between offices. If you are handling it alone, phone the auditor first about the conveyance fee and any county tax, then phone the recorder about page rates and the surcharge.

An inherited house adds steps, because whoever signs needs authority over the estate. Heirs should talk to the court handling the estate before they sign, and ask the title agent which proof the recorder wants attached.

For a seller the order runs like this: contract, title search, drafted deed, signing at closing, auditor's stamp, then filing at the recorder. Fees at the auditor and the recorder are normally settled out of the closing funds, so check the settlement statement for each line before you sign.

sections.h2: What to bring to West Union
sections.html:
Pack your folder before you leave. It should hold the signed deed, with the legal description copied word for word from your own prior deed, plus the statement of value and a way to pay at each window. If you are recording for an estate, add whatever papers show who has authority to sign. Phone ahead about the surcharge so the check is right the first time.

Plan the trip in the right order: auditor first, recorder second. A deed with no auditor's stamp gets turned away at the recorder's window, and you lose a trip. If a title company is closing the sale, hand it the same list and let it confirm each step.

Home values here are modest. The typical owner-occupied house is worth $164,200, rent is about $732 a month, and 71.7 percent of homes are lived in by their owners (2020 to 2024 figures). The county holds 12,808 housing units and about 27,865 people as of July 2025. Median household income is $50,264. West Union is the seat and the largest village.

A river-view lot and a village house can price very differently, so rely on recent nearby sales when you set an asking price.

faqs.q: How do I reach the Adams County recorder by phone?
faqs.a: Dial 937-544-5051 or 937-544-2513. Staff are at 110 West Main Street, Room 133, in West Union, weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.

faqs.q: What will the Adams County recorder charge to file a deed?
faqs.a: Expect $17 plus an equal housing trust fund fee for pages one and two, and $4 plus an equal fee for each page after. A surcharge of up to $5 may sit on top, so ask the recorder for the total.

faqs.q: Is there a county transfer tax on an Adams County sale?
faqs.a: Most sales pay the state-authorized conveyance fee. A county tax is extra and exists only if the commissioners voted for one. Ask the auditor at 937-544-2364.

faqs.q: Who files the statement of value on an Adams County sale?
faqs.a: The buyer or the buyer's representative, at the auditor's office, online or in three paper copies. The seller pays the conveyance fee and any county tax then.

faqs.q: Is a deed from parent to child exempt from the conveyance fee in Adams County?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. Such a gift is on the auditor's exempt list, but you must state the reason on the filing, and recording fees are still due.
